slides.0.title: Crete and the Ionian Islands
slides.0.subtitle: The diversity of island PDOs
slides.1.title: Crete's PDO map
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Red PDOs
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Peza, Archanes, Dafnes and Sitia produce reds; Peza and Sitia also have whites
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Malvasia and Candia
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Malvasia Candia, Malvasia Sitia and Candia cover sweet and other styles
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Sea level to altitude
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Vineyards can exceed 900 m (about 3,000 ft); soils include limestone, slate, calcareous clay and red earth
slides.1.highlights.3.title: PGI Crete
slides.1.highlights.3.content: Most of the island's wine is sold as PGI Crete
slides.1.content: Crete has 7 PDOs (Peza, Archanes, Dafnes, Sitia, Candia, Malvasia Candia, Malvasia Sitia).
slides.2.title: Cretan native grapes
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Vidiano
slides.2.highlights.0.content: White; apricot, lime and pear with chamomile and jasmine, brisk minerality
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Vilana
slides.2.highlights.1.content: White; medium-bodied with tropical fruit, thyme and citrus
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Kotsifali
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Red; fleshy, plum and sour cherry, often used for blending
slides.2.highlights.3.title: Mandilari and Liatiko
slides.2.highlights.3.content: Mandilari is full-bodied, high in acid, earthy with fig; Liatiko works dry or sweet, with leather and fig
slides.2.content: Sitia PDO rules: red at least 80% Liatiko, white at least 70% Vilana.
slides.3.title: The Ionian Islands: Cephalonia
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Robola of Cephalonia
slides.3.highlights.0.content: A dry white from the island's own Robola grape, citrus-driven
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Muscat of Cephalonia
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Mavrodaphne of Cephalonia
slides.3.highlights.3.title: An exception in the PGI system
slides.3.highlights.3.content: The Ionian Islands are the only region with no Regional PGI, though they have PDOs and District and Area PGIs
slides.3.content: Robola belonging to Cephalonia is a classic region-to-grape question.
slides.4.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
Which grape mainly makes Sitia PDO red?
Sitia red is at least 80% Liatiko.
How many PDOs does Crete have?
Peza, Archanes, Dafnes, Sitia, Candia, Malvasia Candia and Malvasia Sitia: seven.
Which island is Robola specific to?
Robola of Cephalonia is the island's own dry white.
